title: The Omer: a trait a week
hook: seven weeks, seven traits: love, strength, balance, endurance, humility, foundation, presence
tomorrow: why read one name, when there are so many?

segments.voice: Yesterday, matzah: one flat bread, affliction and haste in a single verse. Bread of freedom. Passover ends, but a count has already begun.

Countdown apps are for things you're waiting for: a trip, a birthday, the last day of school. The Torah sets a count-up instead. It starts during Passover and runs to the next festival, Shavuot: seven weeks, counted out loud, one night at a time. Counting what? In the Torah, days and weeks toward a harvest offering. Later, the Kabbalists gave each week a second job: one trait of the heart, worked on like a muscle, while ordinary life keeps happening around you.
screen: `NOT A COUNTDOWN. A COUNT-UP.` → `SEVEN WEEKS TO SHAVUOT.` → `ONE TRAIT A WEEK.`

segments.voice: Leviticus gives the count: "And ye shall count unto you from the morrow after the day of rest, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the waving; seven weeks shall there be complete." The sheaf is the omer, a measure of new barley brought as an offering, and the season carries its name. Those who keep the count say a blessing each night and the number: today is so many days of the Omer. Then the mystics added a map. The Kabbalists linked each week to a quality from their teaching about how God's light reaches the world: chesed, love; gevurah, strength and limits; tiferet, balance; netzach, endurance; hod, humility; yesod, foundation; malchut, presence. Inside each week, every day pairs the week's trait with another, so one night is love within strength, another humility within love. You don't need the whole map to use it. Take the week's trait as a lens for whatever the week hands you: a fight, a deadline, someone in the hospital. Love week asks, what's the kind move here? Strength week asks, where's the line? A calendar becomes a slow course in character, ending at the festival of receiving the Torah.
screen: `COUNT SEVEN WEEKS.` · `THE OMER: A SHEAF OF BARLEY.` · `LOVE, STRENGTH, BALANCE… PRESENCE.` · `THE TRAIT IS A LENS.` · then, large: `A TRAIT A WEEK.`

segments.voice: Say a trait out loud, once, slowly: chesed, love, if you're starting at the beginning. Then name one person or one situation this week where you could use it, and say that out loud too. End with one slow breath, and let the word settle.
screen: `SAY THE TRAIT.` · `NAME WHERE IT GOES.` · `ONE SLOW BREATH.`
